content.text: {"label":"sick_wave","explanation":"General has 9 absences logged against about 2.4 usual: 4 called in sick and 5 sent home unwell, logged as late as 14:20. As a result general has 27 agents against 32 expected, with only 26 on phones at 14:15 against 32 planned, and service level has fallen from 94-98% to 49%. Volume is close to forecast for the day (+2.9%). The 14:15 rise (+20%) is modest and spread across reasons, so it is not a demand event. There is no relevant incident (only a branch printer P4) and no marketing entry. Payments is near target and has no unusual absences, so this is a supply problem caused by illness on general.","plan_name":"General sick-wave recovery: top up overtime, defer breaks, protect afternoon capacity","rationale":"About 5-6 agents are missing on general for the rest of the day. The existing overtime offers (3 × 12 offered, about 4.8 accepted each, roughly Rs 10.4k) cover part of the gap. Adding two smaller overtime offers (about Rs 3.7k if 40% accept) keeps total overtime spend under the Rs 15k budget. A free break delay for 14:30-16:00 adds capacity during the current dip; agents already delayed at 12:45 are skipped, so the effect is partial. Cancelling general coaching from 17:00 to the close extends the earlier cancellation at Rs 150 per session hour. A callback option and low-cost chat deflection of balance and offer enquiries reduce peak load.
